segments.text: Fleet Switchboard.
Event-driven coordination for fleets of coding agents.
Running a fleet of coding agents breaks in three places.
Messages play telephone, and lose meaning with every hop.
Work queues behind one agent at a time.
And the glue is a timer that types into terminals, interrupting you, and them.
Fleet Switchboard replaces timers and typing with events, and facts.
A comment, a finished worker, your message: each becomes a fact.
A daemon works out what each agent still needs to hear, and delivers it through the harness's API, never by typing into a pane.
segments.say: A daemon works out what each agent still needs to hear, and delivers it through the harness's A P I, never by typing into a pane.

segments.text: Delivery follows one rule.
While you're talking to an agent, news arrives as a note: it rides along with your next message, and never starts a turn.
When you're away, it's a wake, so work keeps moving.
Unread notes become wakes after ten minutes, and bursts are batched into one message.
Every message names its ask: an Intent line and a Done-when line, written once, carried everywhere.
So reports are checked against what you asked for, and drift stops at the source.
Edit an Intent on GitHub, and your chief of staff sees old and new at once, with a toast.
Your chief of staff stays in conversation with you.
A small decision model reads each message. An unrelated one, while it's busy, gets a decoration: hand off first.
The work moves to a background subagent, and you get your answer without waiting.
Every consequential tool call is judged in context: the role, the ask, and the standing authority.
Four yes-or-no questions, combined in code.
The judge only tightens. Allow can become ask or deny, never the reverse.
GitHub stays the memory.
Webhooks are signed and verified. Agents use plain gh, and the harness signs each comment, so nothing echoes back.
segments.say: Webhooks are signed and verified. Agents use plain G H, and the harness signs each comment, so nothing echoes back.

segments.text: State is almost nothing. Delete it, and nothing that matters is lost.
It's proven the hard way.
Every behavior is a scenario with a control that must fail when its safeguard is off.
Hundreds of tests on fakes, the same scenarios on a real OpenCode and herdr, then a live run with real agents.

Calm agents. Clear intent. Your attention, protected.
